claims.text: The AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock is cobalt-free.
Laser-based additive manufacturing with optimized rapid-solidification parameters will reduce compositional segregation relative to conventional bulk fabrication.
Laser-based additive manufacturing with optimized rapid-solidification parameters will reduce residual stress relative to conventional bulk fabrication.
Laser-based additive manufacturing with optimized rapid-solidification parameters will reduce defect formation relative to conventional bulk fabrication.
Reducing segregation, residual stress, and defects will improve the mechanical integrity of AlCrFeNiSi.
The intervention will produce a more homogeneous microstructure with reduced grain-boundary segregation.
The intervention will produce a microstructure with minimized residual stress.
Rapid solidification limits diffusion in AlCrFeNiSi.
Rapid solidification limits phase separation in AlCrFeNiSi.
Limited diffusion and phase separation result in a more uniform elemental distribution and fewer defects.
Laser-additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi will have higher yield strength than conventionally bulk-fabricated AlCrFeNiSi.
Laser-additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi will have higher ductility than conventionally bulk-fabricated AlCrFeNiSi.
The magnitude of the improvement depends on precise process-parameter optimization.
Direct comparative studies establishing the quantitative improvement are lacking.
